subject: Draft: Islanded Network Delivery Playbook + staffing clarifications
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Islanded Network Delivery Playbook + staffing clarifications

Hi team,

Attached is a first-pass playbook for delivering an "islanded" (VPC/private net) customer deployment — working title: islanded-playbook-v0.1.pdf. The doc bundles the high-level delivery steps, gating criteria, minimal runbook, and a proposed RACI for the pilot lane.

Top items I need from you for tomorrow's sync:
- Karthik: confirm the minimal infra footprint (control-plane endpoints, NAT/egress gating) and whether we can reuse our existing KV cache node for pilot customers or if we need dedicated cache instances.
- Grace: ops/handoff — what on-call rotations do we need to promise for a pilot customer? We should be explicit (SREs vs. product ops vs. customer ops).
- Marissa: procurement/billing — what lead time and budget lines are realistic for partner-hosted network connectivity (e.g., Direct Connect / Interconnect) and any MSA attachments we should push early?

Goal for the sync: agree a minimal commitment (people + infra) so we can send a scoped SOW to ClearSight and get procurement feedback. If we can surface any hard no-go items now, better.

Attachments: islanded-playbook-v0.1.pdf (draft)

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Islanded Network Delivery Playbook + staffing clarifications

Hannah — thanks for the draft. Quick architecture notes from infra that affect the staffing ask:

1) Minimal infra footprint for pilot (assume single-region):
   - 2 x model-serving nodes (gpu-m standard) behind a NATed private subnet
   - 1 x control-plane proxy (customer-managed VPN/PrivateLink to control plane)
   - 1 x small KV cache node if we want isolation (we can *try* to reuse shared cache for one pilot but that reduces isolation and complicates SLAs)

2) Key constraints/questions:
   - If ClearSight requires zero egress (no outbound internet) we need an air-gapped delivery which pushes timeline + 3x infra effort. Need a clear ask from them.
   - Persistent volume performance: for some workloads we may need NVMe-backed volumes. We should flag cost delta.

3) Suggested minimal staffing for a smooth 6-week pilot (on-call expectations in parens):
   - 1 infra engineer (50% for first 4 weeks, 25% for rollout) (on-call: no)
   - 1 runtime engineer (80% first 3 weeks) (on-call: yes, rotation with product runtime team)
   - 1 product ops / delivery PM (100% for 6 weeks) (on-call: no)
   - 1 security/compliance SME for initial network review (ad-hoc)

I uploaded a quick network stencil: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xyz-network-diagram (attachment: network-diagram-v2.png).

Bottom line: Reusing shared KV cache is feasible for an initial validation but we should not commit to it for production or anything with strict data isolation. If procurement/budget pushes back, we can propose a staged approach (shared cache -> dedicated cache after go/no-go).

I'll join the sync at 3pm.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: 
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Islanded Network Delivery Playbook + staffing clarifications

Y'all — quick procurement and commercial notes:

- Budget lead time: partner-managed connectivity (Direct Connect/ExpressRoute) typically needs 6–8 weeks once SOW and network details are final. That aligns with a 6–8 week pilot lead time but only if we lock RAM/IPs and firewall rules up-front.
- Partner MSA: Nimbus Cloud has a partner MSA addendum we can reuse; I've pulled the summary and attached: nimbus-msa-summary.pdf. If ClearSight insists on customer redlines, procurement will need their legal team looped early.
- Cost buckets to be explicit about in the SOW: dedicated KV cache node (monthly), NVMe volumes (if required), partner egress fees, and hourly ERT support for the pilot.

Action for us: I can draft a minimal SOW skeleton if we land on the infra profile today. Also — we should ask ClearSight whether they want quarterly invoicing or milestone invoicing.

One more ask: cc'ing procurement@acme.com was intentional so they have visibility to the bill-of-materials. If anyone thinks that's the wrong email, let me know.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ops Lead <ops-lead@clearsight.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: cloud-partner@nimbuscloud.com
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Islanded Network Delivery Playbook + staffing clarifications

Hannah, Marissa — thanks for the clear draft and the breakdown. A few clarifications from ClearSight's side:

- We can accept a staged approach where the initial pilot reuses shared cache (non-sensitive workloads only). Any HIPAA/PHI-related traffic will require dedicated cache and NVMe drives.
- We do not require full air-gap for the pilot, but we *do* need strict egress controls; no TLS terminations outside the island.
- Nimbus is our preferred connectivity partner; they confirmed a tentative 7-week lead for Direct Connect. I'm looping their cloud-partner rep here to kick off the connectivity checklist.

Next steps as we see them:
1) Redwood to send minimal SOW (list infra + estimated spend) — can you include the staged cache plan?
2) Nimbus to provide expected cutover dates and any special routing ACLs required.
3) Procurement: ClearSight prefers milestone invoicing.

We'll review the SOW once it's in; thanks for moving quickly on this.

— Alex (ops lead)
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Operations | ClearSight Health
ops-lead@clearsight.ai
